name: Infernal Peak
reason: The literal source term 'Purgatory Mountain' was renamed 'Infernal Peak' to preserve the hellish connotation in a Western fantasy register.
description: A forbidding mountain of the Skyreach Sect where rule-breakers are imprisoned; Zane's sister Elara is held captive atop it for years, and freeing her is his driving goal through the early saga. The master sheet also lists it as a mountain/training ground, and key confrontations (including Zane's three-year challenge) are tied to it.

name: Thirteen Palaces
reason: Source term 'Thirteen Palaces' was retained unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: The thirteen great powers of the late-saga upper world (Eps 1032-1320), each led by beings counted among the most powerful in existence. Their strongest disciples cap out at the Soul Sea Realm, and the Mist Palace (source Misty Cloud Palace) is one of them; their warriors carry Grade-Three Divine Weapons and constantly seek chances to test themselves.

name: Great House
issues: Episodes use both 'Great Houses' and the canon term 'Legacy House(s)' interchangeably in the same episode range (e.g. Ep 38-43) for the same aristocratic families — a term-drift/synonym split worth flagging.
reason: The source's great noble families / landowning households were localized as aristocratic 'Houses'; 'Great Houses' is used alongside the canonical 'Legacy Houses' for the top-tier noble families.
description: The powerful aristocratic families of the Empire's Capital, whose pampered scions skip the Gauntlet's Entrance Exam and enjoy boosting items, elite training, and inherited bloodlines. They sit atop a pecking order that common houses cannot challenge, and no enmity between them is ever permanent.

name: Leo
reason: The character's Chinese name Meng Changjun was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Leo' suits the friendly young noble, and the surname 'Brandt' was assigned to render the Meng Family as House Brandt.
description: A Nature Level young noble of House Brandt stationed at Dragon's Keep (source: Meng Changjun of the Meng Family at Dragon Castle). He befriends Zane during the Dragon's Keep arc, is repeatedly stunned by Zane's rapid improvement, and acts as a steadying, well-connected ally.

name: Eliot
reason: The character's Chinese name Zuo Yun was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Eliot', fitting his courteous, diplomatic senior-disciple persona.
description: Misty Peak's long-standing number-one inner disciple, the only talent the peak produced in years, whose own ascent stalled at Consummation (source: Zuo Yun, stuck at peak Xiantian). A diplomat and spear user, he graciously cedes the top disciple rank when Zane's 55,000-point trial score eclipses his, and becomes Zane's ally in the All Peaks Competition.

name: Eliot Zane
issues: Extraction artifact: episodes 240-243 contain adjacent mentions like 'Eliot, Zane made a silent vow' — 'Eliot Zane' is never used as a name.
reason: Not an entity; a tokenization artifact of adjacent mentions of Eliot and Zane.

name: Drake
reason: The source's low-level dragon species, rendered 'Flood Dragon'/'Jiao Dragon' in translation, was localized as 'Drake', the standard Western term for a lesser dragon.
description: A lesser dragon species whose remains carry an oppressive draconic aura; a spear carved from a Drake's spine radiates enough pressure to chill an entire arena crowd. Even so, the Cobalt Dragon in Zane's mind regards a mere Drake's spine as beneath its notice.

name: Drake Bone Spear
reason: Source term 'Flood Dragon Bone Spear' was localized as 'Drake Bone Spear', following the Flood Dragon → Drake species rename.
description: A rune-engraved spear carved from a Drake's spine and strengthened by a secret technique, wielded by Jacob (source: Wang Yun) in the tournament arc around Eps 287-305. Its oppressive dragon-might pressure overwhelms the arena before the weapon is consumed by black fire in the duel against Zane.

name: Janet
reason: The character's Chinese name Ji Nan was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Janet'; the shared Ji surname linking her to Ji Luoxue (localized Sloane) was not carried over.
description: A white-clothed female warrior who joins Zane's group in the late Illusory Battlefield arc (Eps 1265-1315), ranking among the top fighters of the party alongside the short warrior. She deeply idolizes Sloane (source: Ji Luoxue), having witnessed her standing at the top of the last great competition, and recognizes the secret technique Zane learned from her idol.

name: Core Apprentice
reason: An adaptation-coined rank name for the Skyreach Sect; the source has no matching fixed term for the status Luo Zheng gains by being reserved by an instructor ahead of the entrance trial.
description: A privileged apprentice rank of the Skyreach Sect whose status and monthly allocation of Energy Capsules vastly surpass what Outer Disciples receive. Zane is accepted as a Core Apprentice early on through Caleb's favor, which exempts him from participating in The Gauntlet entrance trial.

name: Core Strength Level
reason: The source body-forging stage 'Viscera Refining Realm/Stage' (organ tempering) was renamed 'Core Strength Level' to avoid the clinical term and fit the Western fantasy register.
description: The second-to-last stage of the early body-forging ladder, sitting just below the Marrow Refining Level (Ep 2). Reaching it tempers the body's core and is the milestone Zane targets so he can rescue his sister; it has its own Stone Tablet examination.

name: Core
reason: Generic common noun folding unrelated usages: beast cores (Queen's Core, Inferno Core), a cultivator's enhanced core, and fragments of compound terms like Inner-Core Realm and Violet-Core Physique; not a single entity.

name: Empire
reason: The source's 'Burning Heaven Empire' was simplified to 'the Empire' for the Western fantasy setting, dropping the literal Chinese-style compound name.
description: The ruling nation of the early saga, home to the Capital, the Province of Galeria, the Great Houses, and military outposts like Silverspire in The Crucible. Its imperial judgment halls and army set the political backdrop, and the Skyreach Sect allies with it when needed; weaponsmiths across the Empire forge Mythic and Spirit weapons from Celestial Law.

name: Vesper
reason: The character's Chinese name (Daoist/Immortal Tian Miao) was fully localized to 'Vesper', an evocative single name befitting a long-dead immortal.
description: A deceased immortal whose sealed Celestial Tomb, opened only with nine Enchanted Lamps, drives the arc around Eps 483-560. He recreated the Wheel of Fortune to seek out the luckiest warrior as his inheritor, and his final message, preserved in a crystal ball, greets Zane inside the colossal Tomb.

name: Logan
reason: The character's Chinese name Yun Longtao (Senior Brother Yun Tao) was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Logan', a hard-edged name fitting the dominant duelist.
description: A near-invincible competitor in the Divine Kingdom tournament arc (Eps 800-910) who has comprehended the law of space; his smothering spatial power and signature Spatial Blade (source: Void Slashing Sword) crush opponents like Titus and Willard before they can unleash their strength. His kingdom's rivals dread facing him twice.

name: Mack
reason: The character's Chinese name Hei Ming was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Mack', a blunt name suiting the cold, calculating formation master; his Black Rock Peak became Blackrock Peak.
description: An inner disciple of Blackrock Peak (source: Hei Ming of Black Rock Peak) and a major opponent in the All Peaks Competition arc (Eps 235-255). A master of magic arrays and battle formations, he fights by planting colored formation flags to trap opponents, as in his hexagon trap against Eliot.

name: Lily
reason: The sword spirit's Chinese name Yao Ye ('Demon Night') was fully localized to 'Lily', a delicate feminine name contrasting with her dark, baleful aura.
description: The sword spirit residing in Zane's sword Streamer (source: Sword Spirit Yao Ye), born with a powerful dark aura of Malice and able to manifest as a separate fighter from the moment of her creation. Though she moves with supernatural, viper-precise grace and performs a devastating sword dance, she has no soul of her own; the Demon Night Clan reveres her as their Queen.

name: Saint Lord
reason: The source title 'Saint Lord' (also rendered 'Holy Lord'/'Holy Master' for rulers of the Sacred/Holy Lands) was retained as 'Saint Lord', consolidating the translation variants.
description: The title borne by the supreme rulers of the great Holy Lands, beings so powerful that even Realm Lords treat them with deference. In the Underground Palace arc (Eps 1029-1320), the human and ogre Saint Lords hold an uneasy pact while monitoring the Endless Abyss and the warriors who enter it.

name: Dark Nether Cave
reason: The source location rendered 'Profound Nether Cave'/'Xuanming Cave' was localized as 'Dark Nether Cave', keeping the nether imagery in plainer English.
description: A massive cavern at the very bottom of the Tower in the Cursed Land (Eps 580-837), flooded by a deadly light (source: Mysterious Underworld Death Ray) that periodically weakens. Rich in lucky chances but lethally dangerous, it draws War Lords of every race whenever its red light signals an opening; Yolande guesses it is a battlefield left behind by warring world lords.

name: War Fighter
reason: Coined as the bottom tier of the localized war-rank ladder (War Fighter < War General < War Lord/War Sage), which adapts the source's Chaotic Continent ranks (warrior, War General, War Reverend, War Venerable); the exact source term for the lowest tier is not evidenced.
description: The lowest formal combat rank among the races of the Tower of Sin region (Eps 563-946), itself divided into numbered levels (e.g. seventh-level War Fighter). Masses of War Fighters, such as the Ogre hordes, fight under War Generals and are consistently outclassed by higher ranks in the racial wars.

name: Cursed Land
reason: Source term 'Cursed Land(s)' was retained unchanged, standardized to the singular.
description: The cursed region where the Tower of Sin stands, a melting pot of every race (Eps 568-953). All races built teleportation arrays leading to it that appear ordinary to warriors below War Sage rank, because the land itself curses overpowered intruders to a slow death, filtering out War Sages and above.

name: Ancient Heartstone
reason: The source item rendered variously as 'Life Origin Stone'/'Origin Stone of Life'/'Life Source Stone' was localized as 'Ancient Heartstone', consolidating the translation variants under one evocative name.
description: A rare, immensely valuable ore sought in the Heavenly Feather secret realm arc (Eps 775-935); not as rare as Fire Stones but still a fortune apiece. Randy (source: King Yan) covets them desperately, and gathering as many Ancient Heartstones as possible becomes Zane's chief goal of the expedition.

name: Lewis
reason: The character's source name, translated as 'Red Maple' (Hong Feng), was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Lewis Bailey' rather than kept as a literal nickname.
description: The star pupil of the Providence Sect, hailed as its most outstanding talent in a thousand years (source: Red Maple). Cloaked in black and wielding the Shadow Phantoms technique, he dominates the treasure-chest cliff trial on the Death Road arc (Eps 370-400), starting as Zane's rival before becoming an uneasy ally with a streak of comedic cowardice.

name: Cedric Vance
reason: The character's Chinese name Zong Rui was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Cedric Vance', a scholarly-sounding name fitting the elder master craftsman.
description: Cloud Hall's foremost rune expert and rune-crafter (Eps 421-959), a big shot whom even arrogant disciples cannot afford to offend. Tia entrusts him with researching the order-protecting magic array recovered from the Cloud Road, a sixth-grade sect relic that could make Cloud Hall impervious to attack, and he becomes the natural judge of Zane's far superior divine-texture craft.

name: Queen of Punishment
issues: Source translation titles her 'King of Punishment' despite source context implying a female entity; the adaptation renamed the title to 'Queen', aligning with her actual gender and the Three Queens framing.
reason: The source title 'King of Punishment' was adapted to 'Queen of Punishment' to match the character's female identity and parallel the Three Queens (Life, Punishment, Slaughter).
description: One of the Three Queens revered alongside the Queen of Life and the Queen of Slaughter (Lavender); where Life strengthened their people's bodies, Punishment taught them obedience (Eps 831-1308). Prone to manic laughter and merciless toward defiance, she appears before the Hollow Hall clad in blue Saint Sky Armor wielding the Saint Thunder Meteor Hammer, and her statue-bound counterpart trades barbs with Zane.
